blocks.h2: Is Your Geneva Fireplace Ready for the First Cold Night?
blocks.intro: Geneva homeowners usually call us about one of these in October and November:

tiles.h3: Gas Logs in an Old Hearth That Won't Light
tiles.body: In a converted masonry fireplace, the pilot sits low in the firebox and collects ash, dust and debris. A careful cleaning usually solves it.
Cold air pouring out of a fireplace with gas logs often means the damper clamp is missing or set wrong. That's a safety issue as well as a comfort one.
Dark marks on the brick or mantel mean the flue isn't drawing well or the flame is burning dirty.

tiles.h3: A Unit That Shuts Off by Itself
tiles.body: The safety system is shutting the gas off. A weak thermopile or a vent problem is the usual cause.
Get outside first, then call Nicor Gas or 911. We'll handle the repair once it's safe.

blocks.h2: What We Do for Geneva Gas Fireplaces
blocks.intro: We handle the gas side and tell you when the chimney needs a specialist:

steps.body: We test the pilot, the thermopile output, the valve and the controls and replace only what failed.
Burner, pilot and glass cleaned, logs placed the way the manufacturer intended, every fitting leak-tested and the damper clamp or vent checked.
New gas logs or an insert for a fireplace you no longer want to burn wood in, with the gas supply run and tested. See [gas line installation](/geneva/gas-line-installation).

blocks.h2: Fireplaces in Geneva's Old and New Homes
blocks.intro: In the Central Geneva Historic District, most houses were built between 1840 and 1900. Many of their fireplaces were built for wood or coal and have been converted since. In newer subdivisions on the west side, many homes built after 1990 came with a sealed gas unit.

items.body: Gas logs in a masonry fireplace need the damper held partly open at all times so exhaust can escape. If the clamp was removed during a renovation, it needs to go back on.
Some 19th-century fireplaces are shallow or were built for coal. Not every gas log set fits safely. We'll tell you what works in yours.

items.h3: Sealed Units on the West Side
items.body: Direct-vent fireplaces in newer homes are sealed from the room and vent through the wall. Their parts are widely available, so repairs are usually straightforward.
Any gas fireplace can produce carbon monoxide if it burns or vents poorly. Keep a working detector on every floor.

blocks.h2: Gas Fireplace Questions From Geneva Homeowners

items.q: Does my gas log fireplace need the damper open?
items.preview: Yes. Gas logs in a masonry fireplace need a fixed damper opening.
items.answer: Yes. Vented gas logs need the damper held partly open so combustion gases can leave through the chimney. A damper clamp keeps it from being closed by accident.

items.q: Can a 19th-century fireplace be converted to gas?
items.preview: Often, if the chimney is sound and the firebox is suitable.
items.answer: Often. The chimney has to be in good condition and drawing well, and the firebox has to suit the log set. We handle the gas line and valve and point you to a chimney specialist if the flue needs work.

items.q: Why is my fireplace leaving smoke marks on the brick?
items.preview: Poor draft or a dirty flame.
items.answer: Marks above the opening usually mean the flue isn't drawing well or the gas isn't burning cleanly. Cleaning and adjusting the logs often fixes the flame. A draft problem may need a chimney inspection.

items.q: When should I schedule fireplace service?
items.preview: Early fall, before the heating season.
items.answer: September or early October, so any weak part is found on a mild day instead of the first cold night.

items.q: What does gas fireplace repair cost in Geneva?
items.preview: It depends on the part and the fireplace. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what failed and the type of fireplace. Once we've found the problem, you'll approve a flat-rate price before we replace anything.
